'''Jennifer Anne Thomas''', {{postnominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS|FInstP}}, is a British experimental particle [[physicist]] and professor at [[University College London]].<ref name=UCLprofile/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/J.A.Thomas.1|title=Jennifer Anne Thomas profile|publisher=[[INSPIRE-HEP]]}}</ref> She has been a pioneer in the development of particle detectors, and the recipient of the [[Royal Society of London Michael Faraday Prize|Michael Faraday medal and prize]] in 2018 for her "outstanding investigations into the physics of neutrino oscillations".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Medals for SuperNEMO collaborators|url=https://supernemo.org/supernemo/2018/11/21/medals.html|access-date=2020-08-16|website=supernemo.org}}</ref> 

==Education==
She earned a Bachelor of Science degree with honours from Bedford College, [[University of London]], in 1981. She received her [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] in [[particle physics]] from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1983 for research on [[lepton|semi-leptonic]] decays of heavy [[quark]]s supervised by Michael G. Bowler.<ref name=dphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|title=A study of semi-leptonic decays of heavy quarks|first=Jennifer Anne|last=Thomas|year=1983|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph012146257|oclc=53514253}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref name=UCLprofile>{{cite web|title=Prof Jennifer Thomas|url=https://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=JATHO74|publisher=University College London|access-date=2017-05-13|first=Jennifer|last=Thomas|year=2017}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Thomas held a [[postdoctoral research]] position at Imperial College and [[Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron|Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY)]] in Hamburg from 1983 to 1985. She was a [[CERN]] fellow from 1985 to 1988 and worked there on the Time Projection Chamber (TPC) for the [[ALEPH experiment]]. She was a Wissenschaflicher Angestellter at the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics]] in Munich from 1988 to 1991. She then became a staff scientist at the [[Superconducting Super Collider]] Laboratory in Dallas, Texas. 

In 1994, she returned to Oxford as a Research Officer on the [[MINOS]] proposed experiment, subsequently bringing that experiment to [[University College London]] in 1996,<ref name="UCLprofile" /> and leading the MINOS collaboration since 2010. She was instrumental in broadening the range of the experiment to search for the hypothetical [[Sterile neutrino|sterile neutrinos]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Jennifer Thomas {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jennifer-thomas-13429/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref>

As of 2020 her work centres around the physics of [[neutrinos]]. She is the co-spokesperson for the [[MINOS|MINOS/MINOS+]] experiment and is a member of the [[Neutrino Ettore Majorana Observatory|NEMO-III and SuperNEMO]] experiments,<ref name="cern">{{cite web|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/46879/3|work=[[CERN Courier]]|publisher=cerncourier.com|title=Faces and Places: The Queen honours services to science|year=2011|access-date=23 May 2017|archive-date=26 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826235754/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/46879/3}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal

==Awards and honours==
Thomas was awarded a [[Order of the British Empire|Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire]] in the [[2011 Birthday Honours]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.direct.gov.uk/en/Nl1/Newsroom/DG_197710|title=Queen's Birthday Honours List|year=2011|publisher=Direct.gov.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110907201238/http://www.direct.gov.uk/en/Nl1/Newsroom/DG_197710|archive-date=7 September 2011}}</ref> She was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2017|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2017]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jennifer-thomas-13429/|title=Professor Jennifer Thomas CBE FRS|publisher=royalsociety.org|author=Anon|year=2017|location=London|access-date=2017-05-13}}</ref> She is also a [[Fellow]] of the [[Institute of Physics]] and the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=UCLprofile/> She was the winner of the 2018 Institute of Physics [[Michael Faraday Medal and Prize|Michael Faraday medal and prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/faraday/medallists/page_71675.html|title=2018 Michael Faraday Medal and Prize|last=Physics|first=Institute of|website=www.iop.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-07-26|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726201844/http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/faraday/medallists/page_71675.html}}</ref>
